attribution: Credited to the work the manuscript cites, not to OpenAI or the manuscript's authors. The manuscript says: “The precise estimate above is the parallel repetition theorem of Dinur and Steurer [11, Corollary 1.2].” Its bibliography: “[11] Irit Dinur and David Steurer. Analytical approach to parallel repetition. In Proceedings of the Forty-Sixth Annual ACM Symposium on Theory of Computing, STOC ’14, pages 624–633. Association for Computing Machinery, 2014. Corollary 1.2 and Sections 2.1–2.2 are cited in the author manuscript dated June 10, 2014: https://www.dsteurer.org/paper/productgames. pdf.” Quoted from openai/math (Apache-2.0); AMVO has not consulted or checked the cited work.
scope: Theorem 2.2 (Weighted projection-game repetition) of the manuscript “Perfect completeness for 2-to-1 games” (preprints/Perfect-completeness-for-2-to-1-games-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 105 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 2691ba6bd2ac7159), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 6. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The manuscript presents this as a result of other work, which it uses; the attribution names that work in the manuscript's own words. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let G be any finite projection game with the conventions above. For 0 < g < 1 and every integer k ≥ 1, val(G) ≤ 1 − g =⇒ val(G⊗k ) ≤ (1 − g2 /16)k . (2.1) The bound is uniform in the question sets, answer sets, and probability distribution on edge occur- rences.
